biggest_catch: Wyzant takes 25% of every lesson — and pay only comes twice a month (1st and 15th), so a lesson taught on the 16th waits up to two weeks.
catches: 25% platform commission on your posted hourly rate (you keep 75%).
Semi-monthly payouts: direct deposit on the 1st and 15th; lessons must be submitted 5 business days before the disbursement date to be included.
Lessons must be submitted within 14 days — older lessons cannot be submitted and go unpaid.
Payment requires student payment collection; disputed lessons delay payout.
Approval takes 7–10 business days; you set your own rate but compete with 65,000+ tutors.

eligibility: 18+ and eligible to work in the US; expertise in your subjects; profile approval (7–10 business days).
maximize: Submit every lesson the same day you teach it — Wyzant's own policy says lessons older than 14 days can't be submitted at all, and a lesson has to be in at least 5 business days before the 1st or 15th to make that payout, so same-day submission is the difference between this month's pay and next month's. Price with the 25% cut in mind: set your posted rate so that 75% of it is what you actually want per hour. Respond to new student inquiries fast and collect high ratings — Wyzant's marketplace ranks visible, responsive, well-reviewed tutors higher, and more bookings is the only lever on income here.

steps: Apply as a tutor at wyzant.com and get your profile approved (7–10 business days).
Set your hourly rate (you keep 75%; most tutors post $35–$63/hr per Wyzant).
Get booked by students or apply to posted tutoring jobs.
Teach the lesson; submit lesson details on the platform the same day.
Receive direct deposit on the 1st and 15th (submit at least 5 business days prior to be included).
timing: Semi-monthly direct deposit on the 1st and 15th of each month; lessons must be submitted at least 5 business days before the disbursement date (and within 14 days of the lesson).

costs_and_unpaid_time: No fees; Wyzant takes 25% of every lesson. Unpaid time: the 7–10 business days of profile approval, marketing yourself to win students, and any lesson you submit late (unpaid).
